program_en: B.S.Sc. in Geography and Resource Management
program_chi: 地理與資源管理學社會科學學士
learning_outcomes:
1 1. Major
Programme: Knowledge Students will have a comprehensive understanding of
the various theories and concepts of geography and resource management. Students will have specialized knowledge of a
specific area of concentration in the field of geography and resource
management and developed a capacity to theorize and generalize knowledge
in their area of concentration. Students will have developed a life-long ability to
analyze, explain and reflect on real-world spatial development and
resource management issues covered in the curriculum. Students will have developed a capacity to apply
various theories and methods of geography and resource management in
their further studies and career development. Skills Students will have the ability to apply various
quantitative and qualitative geographical analysis and investigation
techniques to find solutions for practical problems. Students will have developed essential generic
skills such as critical thinking, problem solving and self-managed
learning etc. Students will have possessed communication,
interpersonal and leadership skills that they can apply in real-world
contexts. Values Students will have embraced the perspective of
sustainable development and become sensitive to their responsibilities
with reference to spatial development and resource management issues. Students will have developed a capacity to compare,
contrast and respect the social, economic and environmental values of
places at different geographical scales and the significance of local
and regional culture in the context of globalization. 2. Minor
Programme: (i)  |  Geography and Resource Management
Upon the completion of the Minor Programme, students
will have demonstrated basic understanding of fundamental issues related to
the theories and methods of geography and resource management, acquired generic
analytical and problem solving skills and developed sensitivity towards sustainable
development issues with sufficient depth and at a suitable level to allow
further study in geography and resource management subjects or to pursue a
related career.
(ii)  |  Geo-spatial Science for Sustainability
Upon completion of the Minor Programme, students will be
able to:
1.  |  Master
the core concepts of GIS, remote sensing, spatial analytics, and
sustainability; (K)
2.  |  Gain
knowledge of how geo-spatial science can inform decision-making for
sustainable development; (K)
3.  |  Understand
how to apply spatial data and analysis to address sustainability issues; (K)
4.  |  Acquire
skills in spatial data collection, maintenance and management; (S)
5.  |  Be
proficient in using geo-spatial analysis tools and techniques; (S)
6.  |  Be
able to address economic, social and environmental sustainability
challenges through geo-spatial data analytical methods; (S)
7.  |  Develop
the ability to interpret and visualize geo-spatial data effectively; (S)
8.  |  Be
able to communicate effectively with stakeholders through mapping and data
visualization; (S)
9.  |  Be
able to facilitate and converge diverse ideas into solutions that cater to
the underlying needs and values; (S/V)
10  |  Cultivate
the capacity to work with interdisciplinary teams on sustainability
projects; (S/V)
11.  |  Cultivate
the capacity for life-long learning and a strong sense of commitment to
embodying the values of Diversity, Equity and Inclusion in every step of endeavours towards sustainability goals.
(V)
K = Knowledge outcomes
V= Values and attitude outcomes
S = Skills outcomes
